rationale:
Evidence: the best raced designs (iterations 6 and 8, score 138.6) use five sensors at y=0.08 spanning x=-0.05 to +0.05 m, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], base_speed 1.0, ki 0.5, and kd 0.6 or 0.8. Across 60 trials the oval had 1 finish in 20, s-bend progress was 0.295 and slalom 0.097. Every run still leaves the line at max error about 0.062 m, against a 0.06 m limit. The s-bend logs 1.25 line-loss events per run. Iteration 8 gave metrics identical to iteration 6 to three decimals, so the kp 4.0 to 4.5 and kd 0.6 to 0.8 changes had no measurable effect. Speed (0.9 to 1.6) and gains also failed to move the failure point earlier. Widening the span to +/-0.07 m (iteration 7) hurt, so lateral span is not the lever either. The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), which stays at 0.06 for all body widths up to 0.18 m, so body width gives nothing.

Change: I keep the proven iteration 8 controller (kp 4.5, kd 0.8, ki 0.5, base_speed 1.0), since nothing I changed there moved the result. The one change is the sensor footprint, reduced from 16 mm to 12 mm. A smaller footprint gives a sharper reading at the tape edge: a sensor near the edge reads a tape fraction that changes more steeply with offset, and sensors saturate less when the tape sits under two of them. This should give a cleaner signal near the edge of the line, which is where the robot leaves it, and may cut the line-loss events. Sensor positions and weights are unchanged so the signal scale is the same.

Expected result: line-loss events fall toward 1.0 or below on the s-bend and max error moves closer to 0.06 m. Progress on the s-bend should rise modestly, and the oval finish rate should hold or improve. A completion on the s-bend or slalom is still unlikely this round. If the failure point does not move, the next race should test line_loss handling (search_right) or a lower base_speed in combination with a wider wheel track.
